{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Fish|Fish]]

Although the '''tipitapa''' recipe is a secret, this is the most common substitute to it.

==Ingredients==

=== Salsa ===
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]] (vidalia onions are okay, purple or white onions are also acceptable), [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (85 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] in rings
* [[Cookbook:Vinegar|Vinegar]]
* [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|Brown sugar]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Lemon|Lemon]]

=== Fish ===
* 5 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|virgin olive oil]]
* ½–1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (225–450 g) whole fresh [[Cookbook:Carp|carp]], fully cleaned and scaled
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]

==Procedure==
# Heat the oil in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|pan]] over medium heat. Add onions, and cook until translucent. 
# When the onion is translucent, add tomato slices. Cook for 5 minutes, then add a drop or two of vinegar and a [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of brown sugar. Season to taste with salt. Let it cook for a few more minutes, and set to the side.
# Heat the 5 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the fish to the pan, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] until the skin is crispy (approximately 7 minutes per side).
# Place a rack in a baking pan. Transfer the fish to the rack, and bake about 15 minutes at 350°F (175°C).
# Let the fish cool, then salt to taste and return to its pan. Fry again over low heat for 3 minutes each side while re-heating the salsa.
# Add the salsa on top of the fish, and serve.
